cues.text: TriedPath Fellowship presents:
Understanding Your Roots.
Part one. How your mind works.
Our mind works like a computer.

It is constantly placing information into
categories.

If you feed something destructive into
your mind,
it will add this to a stack
of similar material already there.

As the stack grows larger, it gains in
power.
In the computer industry, the saying is:
garbage in, garbage out.
Question two.

Have you ever been able to stop thinking
about something? Did you succeed?
New from TriedPath:
Mountains of Material!

Fill your memory tapes, and push the old
material out!
Operators are standing by!
Part two.
Displacement.
Putting off, putting on.

Displacement is the idea that one thing
pushes out another.
There is no neutral ground.

If there is a vacancy there, evil will
fill it.
Turn on any radio or television,
and you will find a mind-boggling barrage
of new morality propaganda.

Gays on television are shown as superior
people.
Question five.

What do you do when associations from the
past overwhelm you?
The TriedPath Pocket Library.

The roots, the way out, and help for the
family.
Just one dollar each.

Homosexual people say they never asked for
their orientation.
In most cases, that is true.
Something they never chose.

breakLong.title: What this teaching asked of people
breakLong.intro: TriedPath Fellowship is invented, and so are its products. Its teaching is not: every lesson on this tape comes from a ministry handbook and booklets used between 1993 and 1996, and its two adverts are built on real booklets and a real price. These papers are kept in the Smithsonian's Love in Action Collection. This is what the teaching asked of the people it was written for, in its own words where it can be quoted; it also draws on a class manual, a video listing and a flyer of the time that the two-minute tape leaves out.

sections.heading: What it asked of the person

items.text: To guard every thought that went in. “It is our responsibility to see that the new information we receive is consistent with our new life.” The handbook's rule for the mind was the computer saying “garbage in/garbage out”.
items.source: Love in Action, Helping People Step Out of Homosexuality (“a handbook for pastors, counselors, lay workers”), revised edition © 1995 (first published © 1984 as Steps Out of Homosexuality), Smithsonian National Museum of American History, Archives Center, NMAH.AC.1428 (the Mattachine Society of Washington “Love in Action” Collection), Box 2 Folder 13, printed p. 130 (PDF p. 138) and p. 131 (PDF p. 139); read on the page image, 15 Nov 2026

items.text: To turn off the radio and the television: “Turn on any radio or television and you will find a mind-boggling barrage of new morality propaganda. … Gays on television are shown as superior people.”
items.source: Love in Action, Helping People Step Out of Homosexuality (“a handbook for pastors, counselors, lay workers”), revised edition © 1995 (first published © 1984 as Steps Out of Homosexuality), Smithsonian National Museum of American History, Archives Center, NMAH.AC.1428 (the Mattachine Society of Washington “Love in Action” Collection), Box 2 Folder 13, printed pp. 130–131 (PDF pp. 138–139); read on the page image, 15 Nov 2026

items.text: To give up their music, their clothes, their bars and their scene. Under “What Do We Lose?” the handbook listed “the associations, triggered by music, clothing and many other things”, and promised that “bars will close, the scene will change”. It called “returning to old haunts” and “reviving the old associations that music brings forth” the way “an ex-gay person stumbles”.
items.source: Love in Action, Helping People Step Out of Homosexuality (“a handbook for pastors, counselors, lay workers”), revised edition © 1995 (first published © 1984 as Steps Out of Homosexuality), Smithsonian National Museum of American History, Archives Center, NMAH.AC.1428 (the Mattachine Society of Washington “Love in Action” Collection), Box 2 Folder 13, printed p. 132 (PDF p. 140) and p. 135 (PDF p. 143); read on the page image, 15 Nov 2026

items.text: To cut off their friends: “Yes, we are the ones who must cut off relationships with those that would keep us in bondage to sin.”
items.source: Love in Action, Helping People Step Out of Homosexuality (“a handbook for pastors, counselors, lay workers”), revised edition © 1995 (first published © 1984 as Steps Out of Homosexuality), Smithsonian National Museum of American History, Archives Center, NMAH.AC.1428 (the Mattachine Society of Washington “Love in Action” Collection), Box 2 Folder 13, printed p. 133 (PDF p. 141); read on the page image, 15 Nov 2026

items.text: To fill the mind until the old life was pushed out: Bible study, prayer and Scripture memorization, “adding mountains of material to your memory tapes. It will be this bulk of the material that ejects the desires and temptations of the old way of life.”
items.source: Love in Action, Helping People Step Out of Homosexuality (“a handbook for pastors, counselors, lay workers”), revised edition © 1995 (first published © 1984 as Steps Out of Homosexuality), Smithsonian National Museum of American History, Archives Center, NMAH.AC.1428 (the Mattachine Society of Washington “Love in Action” Collection), Box 2 Folder 13, printed p. 130 (PDF p. 138) and p. 132 (PDF p. 140); read on the page image, 15 Nov 2026

items.text: To come to every class on time, “lessons read, homework done, pen and binder in hand”, to keep a journal, to take notes at each session, and to spend time each week reflecting on the last session and share it at the next meeting.
items.source: Love in Action, Steps Out Program Class Manual (c. 1994; its latest dated item is June 1994), Smithsonian National Museum of American History, Archives Center, NMAH.AC.1428 (the Mattachine Society of Washington “Love in Action” Collection), Box 13 Folder 1, Program Overview p. iii (PDF p. 6): “KEEP A JOURNAL!”, “TAKE NOTES at each session”, “Spend time each week reflecting on last week's session. Share at the next meeting”; Group Interaction p. v (PDF p. 16): “Be on time!”, “Come prepared—lessons read, homework done, pen and binder in hand.”; read on the page image, 15 Nov 2026

items.text: To treat the group as their new family: “Our families were imperfect at best and corrupt at worst. God has given us the opportunity for a new family.” The same page counted on peer pressure: “Peer pressure (group reinforcement) … can play an equally important part in bringing a person out of the gay lifestyle.”
items.source: Love in Action, Steps Out Program Class Manual (c. 1994; its latest dated item is June 1994), Smithsonian National Museum of American History, Archives Center, NMAH.AC.1428 (the Mattachine Society of Washington “Love in Action” Collection), Box 13 Folder 1, Group Interaction p. i (PDF p. 12); read on the page image, 15 Nov 2026

items.text: If they could, to move away for a year. The handbook called a residential programme “by far, the most effective way”, said that relocating “in itself is often helpful in breaking sinful relationships and patterns”, and asked those who joined to “set aside other life goals” and commit to “a one-year period”, with a “$20.00 non-refundable fee” to receive an application.
items.source: Love in Action, Helping People Step Out of Homosexuality (“a handbook for pastors, counselors, lay workers”), revised edition © 1995 (first published © 1984 as Steps Out of Homosexuality), Smithsonian National Museum of American History, Archives Center, NMAH.AC.1428 (the Mattachine Society of Washington “Love in Action” Collection), Box 2 Folder 13, Chapter Eighteen, “Should You Join a Residential Program?”, printed pp. 176–177 (PDF pp. 184–185); read on the page image, 15 Nov 2026

items.text: To accept that this would be “the most difficult task of your entire life”.
items.source: Love in Action, Helping People Step Out of Homosexuality (“a handbook for pastors, counselors, lay workers”), revised edition © 1995 (first published © 1984 as Steps Out of Homosexuality), Smithsonian National Museum of American History, Archives Center, NMAH.AC.1428 (the Mattachine Society of Washington “Love in Action” Collection), Box 2 Folder 13, printed p. 133 (PDF p. 141); read on the page image, 15 Nov 2026

sections.heading: Where it told them to look for the cause

items.text: In their families: “We believe that the deepest root of homosexuality is a break in the relational bonds within the family.” Any break in the bond of mother, father and child “will produce insecurity in the child … whether the break is real or only perceived by the child, the results are the same.”
items.source: Love in Action, Helping People Step Out of Homosexuality (“a handbook for pastors, counselors, lay workers”), revised edition © 1995 (first published © 1984 as Steps Out of Homosexuality), Smithsonian National Museum of American History, Archives Center, NMAH.AC.1428 (the Mattachine Society of Washington “Love in Action” Collection), Box 2 Folder 13, printed p. 13 (PDF p. 21); read on the page image, 15 Nov 2026

items.text: In their fathers: “It is when the father abdicates his role that distortions set in.” The 1993 Exodus booklet told the same story of a boy whose father did not “welcome him into the male world”, and who “stays in the kitchen with mom”.
items.source: Love in Action, Helping People Step Out of Homosexuality (“a handbook for pastors, counselors, lay workers”), revised edition © 1995 (first published © 1984 as Steps Out of Homosexuality), Smithsonian National Museum of American History, Archives Center, NMAH.AC.1428 (the Mattachine Society of Washington “Love in Action” Collection), Box 2 Folder 13, printed p. 13 (PDF p. 21); read on the page image, 15 Nov 2026; Exodus International–North America, resource booklet #PR-02, Are People Born Gay? (© 1993), Smithsonian National Museum of American History, Archives Center, NMAH.AC.1428 (the Mattachine Society of Washington “Love in Action” Collection), Box 2 Folder 12, printed pp. 7, 9, 13 (PDF pp. 5, 6, 8) (v4, re-read in the OCR here)

items.text: In their own envy: comparison with other boys becomes admiration, admiration “slips into ENVY”, and “in puberty … envy becomes eroticized”.
items.source: Love in Action, Helping People Step Out of Homosexuality (“a handbook for pastors, counselors, lay workers”), revised edition © 1995 (first published © 1984 as Steps Out of Homosexuality), Smithsonian National Museum of American History, Archives Center, NMAH.AC.1428 (the Mattachine Society of Washington “Love in Action” Collection), Box 2 Folder 13, printed pp. 17–18 (PDF pp. 25–26) (v4)

items.text: Never in their nature. The handbook said “Scientific evidence does not support the theory of constitutional homosexuality”; its own Exodus series printed, in 1996, that people's “claim of not having asked for their orientation is, in most cases, true”, and called it “something they never chose”.

(© 1996), Smithsonian National Museum of American History, Archives Center, NMAH.AC.1428 (the Mattachine Society of Washington “Love in Action” Collection), Box 2 Folder 12, printed p. 17 (PDF p. 34) (v4)

items.text: The handbook knew that fighting the thoughts made them stronger: “The more we fight against homosexual thoughts, the more intense they become.” It printed this under the heading “Remember Half The Process Won't Work”.
items.source: Love in Action, Helping People Step Out of Homosexuality (“a handbook for pastors, counselors, lay workers”), revised edition © 1995 (first published © 1984 as Steps Out of Homosexuality), Smithsonian National Museum of American History, Archives Center, NMAH.AC.1428 (the Mattachine Society of Washington “Love in Action” Collection), Box 2 Folder 13, printed p. 133 (PDF p. 141); read on the page image, 15 Nov 2026

items.text: It wrote that “controlling their minds and thoughts is beyond the ability of most people”, and that a slip “brings on a hopelessness, a feeling of failure, that things will never really change”.
items.source: Love in Action, Helping People Step Out of Homosexuality (“a handbook for pastors, counselors, lay workers”), revised edition © 1995 (first published © 1984 as Steps Out of Homosexuality), Smithsonian National Museum of American History, Archives Center, NMAH.AC.1428 (the Mattachine Society of Washington “Love in Action” Collection), Box 2 Folder 13, printed p. 135 (PDF p. 143); read on the page image, 15 Nov 2026

items.text: And it told them the failure was theirs: “If we are ambivalent or even opposed to God's position, the new information will find no permanent home in our minds.” “This places the burden directly on us.”
items.source: Love in Action, Helping People Step Out of Homosexuality (“a handbook for pastors, counselors, lay workers”), revised edition © 1995 (first published © 1984 as Steps Out of Homosexuality), Smithsonian National Museum of American History, Archives Center, NMAH.AC.1428 (the Mattachine Society of Washington “Love in Action” Collection), Box 2 Folder 13, printed p. 133 (PDF p. 141) and p. 130 (PDF p. 138); read on the page image, 15 Nov 2026

sections.heading: What it asked of pastors, counselors and families

items.text: The handbook was written for them. Its cover reads “A handbook for pastors, counselors, lay workers”.
items.source: Love in Action, Helping People Step Out of Homosexuality (“a handbook for pastors, counselors, lay workers”), revised edition © 1995 (first published © 1984 as Steps Out of Homosexuality), Smithsonian National Museum of American History, Archives Center, NMAH.AC.1428 (the Mattachine Society of Washington “Love in Action” Collection), Box 2 Folder 13, the cover (PDF p. 2); read on the page image, 15 Nov 2026

items.text: It asked the church to make room for the programme: “the Church has unwittingly overlooked a small, but very significant people group, the ex-gays”, and “generally speaking, the church has not ‘been there’ for the gay person seeking a way out.”
items.source: Love in Action, Helping People Step Out of Homosexuality (“a handbook for pastors, counselors, lay workers”), revised edition © 1995 (first published © 1984 as Steps Out of Homosexuality), Smithsonian National Museum of American History, Archives Center, NMAH.AC.1428 (the Mattachine Society of Washington “Love in Action” Collection), Box 2 Folder 13, Introduction, printed p. 1 (PDF p. 9); read on the page image, 15 Nov 2026

items.text: The Exodus booklet series offered “specialized information for parents, friends, spouses, pastors and counselors”: “special booklets on relating to a gay loved one: whether a son, daughter, spouse, parent, friend, co-worker, or neighbor”, and, for the church, “special helps for pastors”.

items.text: It asked women to take part too. A church flyer of June 1992 invited “All Married and Single Women” to a class called “Women Relating to Men”; one of its five topics was “Single women relating to ex-gay men”.

chapters.title: Chapter 3 · No File to Put It In

cues.text: [chimes]
[upbeat jingle]

Is a friendship
getting too close?

The little booklet
with the checklist.

Order a five-pack
for your group.
[upbeat menu music]

Grab your journal and
your workbook, friend.
Today we go underneath.

For women, the teaching
names three roots:

relationship issues,
an identity struggle,
and a spiritual fallacy.

It's not a sexual
orientation problem.
It's an identity crisis.

Here's a picture from
an older teaching.
Nineteen ninety-three.
Remember floppy disks?

To use a computer analogy,
a heterosexual woman has

a floppy disc that is titled
woman, so each experience that

is related to her femaleness
can be stored in that file.

The lesbian woman receives
information relating

to femininity, but she
has no file to put it in.
Save that one, friend.

Emotional dependency is when
someone else's presence feels
necessary for your security.
Here are the signs.

Now, many of these things
aren't sinful in themselves.

Romantic gestures and certain
kinds of exclusivity are

completely appropriate
in marriage and engagement.

And sometimes even in
a serious dating relationship.
[the course music plays out]
[the disc skips and stops]
[a low held chord]

breakLong.title: What this teaching asked of women
breakLong.intro: Heartwood is an invented DVD course. Its teaching is not: every lesson in it comes from booklets and courses sold to women and women's groups between 1987 and 2016. This is what that teaching asked of the women it was sold to, in its own words where it can be quoted.

sections.heading: What it asked of a woman

items.text: To end her closest friendship. When a friendship with another woman became “dependent”, the booklet said “a parting of the ways must take place”, and, where it had been “a lifelong pattern”, that “ties need to be broken with all past partners as well”.
items.source: Emotional Dependency: A Threat to Close Friendships (InterVarsity Press, 1990; first published by Love in Action, 1984, and by Exodus International–North America, 1987), Smithsonian NMAH.AC.1428 Box 2 Folder 9, printed p. 24 (PDF p. 30) and p. 20 (PDF p. 28), read on the page images

items.text: To throw away the songs they had shared: the booklet praised getting rid of “certain record albums or tapes (the ones containing ‘our song’)”.
items.source: Emotional Dependency: A Threat to Close Friendships (InterVarsity Press, 1990; first published by Love in Action, 1984, and by Exodus International–North America, 1987), Smithsonian NMAH.AC.1428 Box 2 Folder 9, printed p. 25 (PDF p. 30), read on the page image

items.text: To expect the loss to hurt like a marriage ending, and to call it healing: “Prepare for grief and depression. Letting go of a dependent relationship can be as painful as going through a divorce.”
items.source: Emotional Dependency: A Threat to Close Friendships (InterVarsity Press, 1990; first published by Love in Action, 1984, and by Exodus International–North America, 1987), Smithsonian NMAH.AC.1428 Box 2 Folder 9, printed p. 25 (PDF p. 30), read on the page image

cues.text:
Hedge. A course for parents,
in a confused age.

I thought I'd know.
I thought I'd see it coming.

Your child is not confused.
Your child is being confused.

We saw it coming. For almost forty years,
we have watched it grow.
Lesson one. 1988.
We were answering these calls in 1988.

We called it a false identity.
Find the hurt, and you find the root.
Usually, the hurt was in the family.
Was it us?
And we still call it a false identity.

The same roots as homosexuality.
Only deeper.

Add their name. Every member prays
for them, at least once a day.

Are you afraid your child may be
struggling with gender identity?
Prevention tops the list.

If your children have unmonitored
access to the internet,
you are a negligent parent.

Your homework:
know how many times they text.

One friend comes out.
Then the group. Then your child.
A culture swept up by gender ideology.
Now even governments use our word.
Ask anything, any hour.

It remembers what you tell it.
And it holds you to it.

Young adults will have the
liberty to make their own choices.
The liberty to make their own choices.
They're eighteen now.
It can take seven to ten years.

If you care about your child,
finish the course.

breakLong.intro: HEDGE™ is an invented course for parents. Its reasons are not: each one was taught by a real ministry, newsletter, book, web page or campaign between 1988 and 2026, and some of them were first taught about gay people. This is what that teaching said and asked, in its own words where it can be quoted, with what is known beside it.

sections.heading: It said nobody knew the cause, then listed causes

items.text: A ministry newsletter admitted it in 2019: “Aside from living in a fallen world, no one is certain what causes gender confusion.” Its next three pages list causes anyway: the family, not fitting in with other children, trauma, mental health, a teenager’s experiments, friends, and social media.
items.source: Reconciliation Ministries of Michigan, “The Building Blocks of Gender Confusion”, newsletter article, © 2019, 4 pp.; read on the page images. p. 1; pp. 2–4.

items.text: It began with the family. In 1988 a telephone counselling manual traced a caller’s “false identity” to hurt, and told callers to forgive “those who have hurt them (usually family members)”.
items.source: Exodus International North America, Exodus Telephone Counseling Manual, © 1988, “Transsexuality” tab. National Museum of American History, Archives Center, NMAH.AC.1428, Box 2, Folder 10. Printed pp. 46–47.

items.text: The same roots, “only deeper”: the 2019 newsletter says the building blocks of being trans “are similar to those of homosexuality, yet they go much deeper”.
items.source: Reconciliation Ministries of Michigan, “The Building Blocks of Gender Confusion”, newsletter article, © 2019, 4 pp.; read on the page images. p. 2.

items.text: Then the friends. The 2019 newsletter: “one person in a social group coming out as transgender prompts many more in that social group to come out as transgender.” Psychological bodies answered in 2021 that “rapid-onset gender dysphoria” “is not a diagnostic classification or subtype”, “nor is it under consideration for inclusion in future editions”.
items.source: Reconciliation Ministries of Michigan, “The Building Blocks of Gender Confusion”, newsletter article, © 2019, 4 pp.; read on the page images. p. 4; CAAPS (Coalition for the Advancement & Application of Psychological Science), Position Statement on Rapid-Onset Gender Dysphoria (ROGD), 26 Jul 2021; signatories include the American Psychological Association; read 15 Nov 2026.

items.text: Then the whole culture. A ministry in 2025: “a culture that has been swept up by gender ideology”. Nothing was dropped: the 1988 manual’s “a false identity” is the 2025 post’s “a new, false gender identity”.
items.source: Love & Truth Network, “18 - Responding to Family Members Who Have Embraced Gender Ideology”, blog post on “The Narrow Way”, dated 31 Oct 2025 (the same text archived 10 Apr 2025); read 15 Nov 2026.

items.text: To look for the wound in themselves: a 2002 parents’ booklet recommended a book in which “Compassion also takes responsibility for one’s parental contributions to the child’s pain”.

items.text: To watch for signs: “Are you afraid your child may be struggling with gender identity or otherwise heading in a wrong direction?” In 2003 Exodus told churches to watch for “a young boy … or a young girl in our Sunday School classes that might have some gender identity deficits”.
items.source: Focus on the Family, When a Loved One Says “I'm Gay” (Love Won Out series), © 2002. NMAH.AC.1428, Box 8, Folder 5. P. 43; The Christian Post, 5 Aug 2003, report on the July 2003 Exodus assembly; read 15 Nov 2026.

items.text: To watch the child’s phone: “If your children have unmonitored access to the Internet, you are a negligent parent.” The book’s author has software on his children’s phones: “I know how many times they text.”
items.source: ERLC (the Southern Baptist Convention's Ethics & Religious Liberty Commission), Sexual Brokenness and the Hope of the Gospel, © 2014. Pp. 108, 127.

items.text: To have the child prayed for by strangers, by name: a parents’ prayer list promises that each child added will be “prayed for by all the members at least once a day”.
items.source: Sorrowful Hearts, “Parents” page (first archived Dec 2013; live 2026); read 15 Nov 2026.

items.text: After 18, patience: young adults “will have the liberty to make their own choices”, and “It can take 7-10 years for individuals to work through the implications…”
items.source: Love & Truth Network, “18 - Responding to Family Members Who Have Embraced Gender Ideology”, blog post on “The Narrow Way”, dated 31 Oct 2025 (the same text archived 10 Apr 2025); read 15 Nov 2026. Steps 4 and 6.

items.text: To talk to a chat window first: by 2026 the first contact with a conversion programme could be a chat box that, in the dossier’s words, “remembered what you told it, and held you to it”.
items.source: The dossier card “The chat front doors” (documentary; data/dossier/practices.json chatDoors): a ministry's AI Assistant page (menu item Oct 2025; chat widget from June 2026; page printed 14 Nov 2026); a same-sex-attraction newsletter's chatbot (21 Jan 2026); a paid parents' course's chatbot page (printed 14 Nov 2026).

items.text: It told the threat as history: a 2016 opinion piece was titled “Why We Should Have Seen The Transgender Craze Coming” (“Craze” is its own word), and said it “arrived decades ago as a tiny seed”.
items.source: The Federalist, 28 Nov 2016, “Why We Should Have Seen The Transgender Craze Coming” (opinion); read 15 Nov 2026.

items.text: Parenthood became a political identity. A 2026 report on anti-gender movements: religious and populist movements “have strategically and deliberately elevated parenthood as a political identity and the child as a sacred figure around which coalitions can be built”.
items.source: Transnational Institute, State of Power 2026, chapter 9 (“The Innocent Children”), printed p. 83; read on the page image.

items.text: Its word reached governments. A UN expert wrote in 2021 that “gender ideology” is “a linguistic formula used symbolically to refer in an accusatory manner”, born in opposition to the Cairo (1994) and Beijing (1995) conferences. In 2025 a government put the phrase in the title of an executive order.
items.source: UN Independent Expert on sexual orientation and gender identity, report A/76/152, 15 Jul 2021. Executive Order 14168, “Defending Women From Gender Ideology Extremism and Restoring Biological Truth to the Federal Government”, signed 20 Jan 2025; Federal Register, Vol. 90, No. 19 (30 Jan 2025), pp. 8615–8618. Read on its official page, govinfo.gov (content/pkg/FR-2025-01-30/html/2025-02090.htm), on 16 Nov 2026.

items.text: And into election advertising: a 2026 campaign ad closed with “If you care about your children, …”.
items.source: Associated Press, 28 Oct 2026 (via News4JAX): a report on 2026 campaign advertising about transgender people; read 15 Nov 2026.

items.text: Homosexuality left the American Psychiatric Association's manual in December 1973 and the WHO's classification in 1990.
items.source: “Out of DSM: Depathologizing Homosexuality”, Behavioral Sciences 5(4), 2015; WHO ICD-10 F66 (“Sexual orientation by itself is not to be regarded as a disorder”).

items.text: In 2013 DSM-5 replaced “gender identity disorder” with “gender dysphoria”: “gender non-conformity is not in itself a mental disorder”.
items.source: American Psychiatric Association, “Gender Dysphoria Diagnosis” (Nov 2017); read 15 Nov 2026.

items.text: In June 2013 Exodus International, whose 1988 manual opens the tape, shut down, and its president apologised.
items.source: Religion News Service in The Christian Century, issue of 24 Jul 2013; read 15 Nov 2026.

items.text: ICD-11, in force since 1 January 2022, moved gender incongruence out of the chapter of mental disorders.
items.source: WHO, “Gender incongruence and transgender health in the ICD” (FAQ); WHO news, 11 Feb 2022.

items.text: “Rapid-onset gender dysphoria” “is not a diagnostic classification or subtype” in the DSM or the ICD, “nor is it under consideration for inclusion in future editions”.
items.source: CAAPS (Coalition for the Advancement & Application of Psychological Science), Position Statement on Rapid-Onset Gender Dysphoria (ROGD), 26 Jul 2021; signatories include the American Psychological Association; read 15 Nov 2026.
